fixes.explanation: You've got it, baker. God says, "…you bathed for them, painted your eyes, and adorned yourself with jewelry." The sisters get ready for the men who came from afar, the way you'd get ready for company. They sent messengers for those men, and then they got dressed up for them.
Gold and silver aren't what the verse names. God says what was set on the table was "…My incense and My oil…" Those are the things He calls His own in this verse.

Yes. The mob will "…and burn down their houses." It's a heavy verse. The same verse says they will stone the sisters, cut them down with swords and kill their sons and daughters. I think this is one of the places in the passage where it's right to go quiet for a second.
Moving in isn't what the verse says. It says the mob will "…and burn down their houses." The word is burn, not move into. It's a heavy picture of the judgment.

You nailed it. God ends with, "Then you will know that I am the Lord GOD." The whole passage closes on who He is. The sisters will bear the consequences of their sins of idolatry, and then they will know Him.
Egypt isn't mentioned in this verse. It says nothing about anyone rescuing the sisters. God says, "Then you will know that I am the Lord GOD."
